title: 表示定理：有限读取通向有限系数求解
caption: 有界线性读取 L_i 在 Hilbert 空间中有 Riesz 表示元 h_i。将 f 分解为 M=span{h_i} 中的分量与正交分量后，所有读取只依赖 f_M；去掉 f_⊥ 不增加范数正则项。令 f_M=Σ_j a_jh_j 后，读取与范数分别写为 Ga 与 aᵀGa，便得到有限系数问题。该结论不单独保证最优解存在，也不保证 Gram 矩阵奇异时系数唯一。 下方曲线只表示求解操作，不声称实际有限目标为二次函数或总有唯一最小点。
brief: Scientific mechanism: in a Hilbert space, n bounded linear readouts have Riesz representer vectors h_i. Their span is a finite subspace M. Any candidate function f decomposes into f_M plus f_perp, orthogonal to M. The perpendicular part is invisible to ALL readouts, yet only adds nonnegative squared norm. Thus removing f_perp keeps readings unchanged and does not increase a nondecreasing norm penalty. A candidate in M is a linear combination of the h_i with finite coefficients a. Gram matrix G converts coefficients into the n readout values Ga, and its quadratic form gives squared norm a-transpose G a. These two streams feed a finite coefficient optimization problem. Make an explanatory mechanism illustration combining a simple flat orthogonal-vector construction (exact right-angle geometry, NO 3D plane or perspective) and a clearly related finite interface/Gram-to-solver mechanism. Draw one original vector, its projection along a finite-span baseline, and orthogonal dashed component from projection tip to original tip. Do not imply Hilbert space itself has dimension n. Finite reading channel can be a set of 3 small representative ports plus an empty continuation gap, not falsely depicting exactly three samples as mathematical n. There is a distinct Gram/coefficient interface and a solver output with reserved labels; show readings and norm entering the finite objective. No unconditional guarantee of existence or uniqueness, and no fake numerical solution. All mathematical labels/formulas added later, leave clean blank spaces next to vectors, reading channels, Gram module and solver. Prefer mostly white with pale Blue geometry, Green reading path and Orange finite objective, very few icons. The reference perspective feature-space sketch is conceptual only; our figure must be flat2D.
